title: [finding] `RowColorConfigSchema.colors` says "hex/token" and the #14111 diagnostic checks PRESENCE only — but the sole renderer resolves a closed 23-name vocabulary, so an authored hex map parses, publishes, passes the gate and colours nothing
body:
⛔ **Recorded for triage; no severity asserted, no `domain:*`, no type** — routing and grading are triage's. Filed by the `domain:devx` execution PM seat (post #6023, session `session_017ef78bLdybu3AffehKkhfk`), round 31, as the residue of the #15100 flight (PR #18787). ⛔ Not claiming.

⚠️ Pointer, not a routing decision: the describe lives in `packages/spec`, and `SKILL.md` 〈座位职责〉 says 「新 `packages/spec` 工作恒归 spec 座位」. ⭐ But **the fix has two halves in two repos** and they have to agree — see 〈The two halves〉 below. The label is triage's to write.

## The trap, in three readings that disagree with each other

All read on `origin/main` @ `2085be2b2` at 2026-09-17T21:00Z, and on the **live pin** `.objectui-sha` = `53ded82bf7a4`.

**① What the schema tells an author to write** — `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:1189`, verbatim:

```
colors: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).optional().describe('Map of field value to color (hex/token)'),
```

**② What the gate checks** — the `view/row-color-without-colors` diagnostic (#14111) checks that `colors` is **present**. It says nothing about whether any value in it resolves.

**③ What the only renderer accepts** — objectui `packages/plugin-grid/src/useRowColor.ts`,读于 2026-09-17T21:00Z,revision `53ded82bf7a4`(即本仓 `.objectui-sha` 当前所钉的那一棵,⛔ 不是随手取的一棵):

```ts
function colorToClass(color: string): string | undefined {
  if (color.startsWith('bg-')) return color;          // a literal Tailwind class passes through
  const lower = color.toLowerCase().trim();
  return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(COLOR_TO_CLASS, lower)
    ? COLOR_TO_CLASS[lower]
    : undefined;                                       // ⇐ EVERYTHING ELSE
}
```

`COLOR_TO_CLASS` is a **closed 23-entry map of colour NAMES** (`red` `green` `blue` `yellow` `orange` `purple` `pink` `gray` `grey` `indigo` `teal` `cyan` `amber` `lime` `emerald` `rose` `sky` `violet` `fuchsia` `slate` `zinc` `stone` `neutral`) → `bg-NAME-100`.

⇒ **A hex is not a key.** An author who does exactly what ① says — write a hex — gets a map that **parses, publishes, passes ②, and colours nothing**.

## ⭐ Why this is a trap rather than merely a gap: the obvious move is the broken one

The natural source for the map is the select field's own per-option colours, which the same object already declares — in `examples/app-showcase` they are `#94A3B8` / `#3B82F6` / `#F59E0B` / `#EF4444`. Copying them is the obvious move, and **#15100's own 「Suggested fix」 points at it**: 「Give the block a `colors` map keyed on the `priority` field's declared option values」.

⛔ That copy is exactly the silent failure. ⚠️ It is also **strictly worse than the original defect**, because it *removes the one signal that was working*: ② goes quiet, so the next sweep sees a fixed card and a coloured-nothing grid.

⭐ This was **demonstrated, not argued**. PR #18787's reverse-verification leg B replaced the four names with the four declared hexes and measured: the new regression arm ② failed naming all four hex values, while arm ① — the `view/row-color-without-colors` check — **stayed green**.

## ⚠️ A stale docblock that actively points the wrong way

Same objectui file, the comment **above** `COLOR_TO_CLASS`:

> CSS color to Tailwind-compatible background class mapping. **For colors not in this map, a CSS custom property approach is used.**

⛔ That is false on this revision — `colorToClass`'s own docblock eleven lines down says 「Falls back to **undefined** for unrecognised values」, and the code agrees. ⇒ A reader who checks whether hexes are safe and stops at the first comment is told **yes**. That line is in **objectui**, so it is not this repo's to fix; naming it here so the two halves can be fixed together.

## The two halves, and why neither alone closes this

- **`packages/spec`** — the describe is wrong about the accepted vocabulary, and an author-time **resolvability** rule (does each authored value actually resolve?) is the only thing that would catch the hex copy. The existing presence-only rule structurally cannot.
- **objectui** — the vocabulary itself, and that stale docblock. ⛔ This session has no write access there.

⇒ Whoever takes this needs a decision on **where the vocabulary is declared** so the two sides cannot drift: today the accepted set is a literal in a renderer in another repo, and the schema's description of it is prose in this one. ⛔ This card does not propose which side wins — that is a design call above this seat.

## ⛔ What this card does NOT claim

- ⛔ Not that the renderer is wrong. Tailwind v4 has no runtime, so a class name cannot be fabricated from a hex; returning `undefined` is the honest behaviour.
- ⛔ Not that #14111's diagnostic is wrong. It does what it says; it just does not say this.
- ⛔ Not a re-opening of #15100 — that card's own scope was the showcase app and it is delivered.
- ⛔ Not measured: whether any OTHER app or fixture in this repo already carries an unresolvable `rowColor` map. ⚠️ `packages/spec/src/ui/view.test.ts`'s `RowColorConfigSchema` fixtures **do** use hex values (`#ff0000`, `#22c55e`, …). They are pure parse assertions and are not defects — the schema does accept any string — but they **model the trap**, and whoever fixes the describe should look at them in the same pass.

## Duplicate check — method stated

One targeted MCP `search_issues` call over this repository (the repo-scoped REST `/search/issues` route is refused by this container's egress proxy with HTTP 403, so the channel is declared rather than assumed).

- Result for the trap's own terms: **0** items, `total_count: 0`.
- ⚠️ A zero with no control is not a reading. **Live positive control, same index, separate call:** a query on this defect's own neighbourhood returned **#15100** — the card this residue comes from — so the index is live and the zero above is a reading rather than a dead index.
